This is a fifth reachable trigger absent from f5's enumerated set (rebase gap, null/absent boundary, regression, duplicate slot), and none of the four frozen families addresses it: a per-source supersession commitment, a settled prefix keyed on skipped sources, an accumulator over sources, and any construction from existing signed vertex identities all settle rows the creator never saw, whereas here the creator did see the row and simply cannot reach it again. An f5 GREEN built to the current plan would leave this path stalled.
findings.required_action: Amend D.110c-0c1f5 to add this trigger to the demonstrated product paths and to the causal RED matrix (creator admits sequence n+1 in epoch k, admits n in epoch k+1, then closes at least twice more; prove the boundary freezes below n+1 and the writer's cold reopen refuses), and require the selected construction to make any sequence the creator itself admitted in any prior close reachable by the boundary. Do not add a bare observed maximum and do not add an O(epoch) or O(hole) uncounted store.

structured_output.selected_design: Selected: a bounded settled RUN, not a settled prefix over sources. Replace the per-author 2-tuple `[author, admittedAuthorSequence]` with the 3-tuple `[author, coveredFromSequence, admittedAuthorSequence]`, where both numbers are null-or-safe-integer and the attested covered set is exactly the closed interval [coveredFromSequence, admittedAuthorSequence]. The creator advances the run through adjacent sequences it observed in the current close graph exactly as today; when it observes a contiguous run that does not adjoin the prior boundary, it may START A NEW RUN at that run's first sequence instead of stalling, publishing the new floor. Every element of the interval is a sequence the creator itself admitted, so this is strictly a subset of "creator observed it" and is not a bare maximum: an unseen or substituted row below the floor is outside the interval and stays fail-closed. Rows orphaned below the floor are not silently dropped; `authenticatedCoveredHistoricalOutboxRow()` returns undefined for them and recovery surfaces them as an explicit per-row held/refused disposition to the application instead of failing the whole reopen. WHO AUTHENTICATES WHAT: only the creator, from the pinned trust root already in use — the aggregate is signed under domain `ts-drp/creator-author-issuance-frontiers/v1` and verified against an independently authenticated successor anchor floor; no author-signed supersession statement, no new signer, no new trust root, no application field. HOW CLOSE VERIFIES WITHOUT TRUSTING STORAGE: unchanged. `writeAuthorizedAuthors()` derives the writer set from the successor snapshot ACL opened against the successor anchor digest; the prior aggregate is opened via `openCreatorAuthorIssuanceFrontiers()` against the current floor, the closure's cut/QC/ACL candidates and the expected manifest digest; observations come only from `captureCloseGraph()`, which is the creator's own admitted graph; remote durable stores are never read. The transition verifier keeps `priorAggregateCandidateDigest === current.ref.digest`, the genesis sentinel only when no prior aggregate exists, and the conditional legacy/aggregate creator equality; its monotonicity rule extends to "the run may move up but never down and never widens below its floor". EDGE CASES: null boundary and null floor mean no covered history and nothing is covered. Absent prior-author entry, first observed sequence greater than one, a sequence at or below the numeric boundary, and a duplicate (author, sequence) slot all become per-author fail-closed dispositions that leave that author's entry unchanged or null and let the close proceed for everyone else — never a close-wide throw. A numeric gap opens a new run above it. A regression is refused for that author only. Crash before reissue leaves the source pending and below no floor, so nothing settles. Crash after reissue but before source completion leaves the source pending below the new floor; it is refused, held and reported, never authenticated and never silently settled. Replay, substitution and forks fail the existing signature/digest/preimage checks. Cross-author, cross-object and cross-epoch material fails the existing object/author/anchor/epoch identity checks and the `epoch < closedEpoch` test. Restart re-opens the same signed aggregate, so every consumer agrees. RETENTION AND PRUNING: exactly one aggregate is live; close removes the prior candidate from the closure and stages one successor, so replacement stays O(1) and the previous generation is retained only by the existing rollback/availability window. GROWTH: proof and active control state grow with neither authors beyond the existing 64-member ACL cap, nor gaps, nor rebases, nor epochs; the record adds one integer per author. COMPARISON: family 1 is rejected because binding each skipped source to its replacement needs a statement only the author can make, which is a new signed carrier and a new authority; family 3 is rejected because membership or consistency proofs need a retained per-epoch index and age-growing proofs that Phase 6 does not have and that violate the bounded-ordinary-reopen constraint; family 4 is rejected because I confirmed no existing material carries the fact — the reissued vertex takes its dependencies from the current frontier (`examples/v3-room/src/index.ts` sets explicit dependencies only for the pinned-genesis bootstrap), so no signed preimage, displaced-operation identity, close-set or history commitment binds a replacement to its source. PREREQUISITE: the 3-tuple is an additive change to the canonical signature preimage of `drp-creator-author-issuance-frontiers-state`, so it is a carrier/schema change and f5 RED stays unauthorized until it is opened as its own high-risk prerequisite; because the carrier was introduced in the unreleased commit 9e1781e0 and no room has adopted it, that prerequisite needs no migration protocol, no dependency, no threshold change and no public room API change, and the deterministic maximum-shape encoder must re-prove the 64-entry worst case below the unchanged 8,192-byte ceiling (currently 6,241 bytes; the third element adds roughly 1.2 KB worst case) and stop and reslice rather than raise the ceiling if it does not fit. RED SHAPE ON THE REAL PRODUCT PATH: the close-liveness half needs no carrier change at all and can go RED immediately using only existing primitives — one genuine noncreator writer produces each of the null, absent, at-or-below-boundary and duplicate-slot shapes through ordinary offline and rebase behaviour, each is asserted to abort the creator's whole close today at the exact current message while the no-gap control stays green, and the tests emit `D110C_0C1F5_FOREIGN_AUTHOR_CLOSE_LIVENESS_REQUIRED`. The supersession half's RED (`D110C_0C1F5_REBASE_SUPERSESSION_FRONTIER_REQUIRED`) is authorable only after the carrier prerequisite is reviewed, and must also cover the cross-epoch out-of-order trigger in P1 #2.
structured_output.consumer_authority_contract: `authenticatedCoveredHistoricalOutboxRow()` (`packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:4733-4795`) grants exactly this and nothing more: given a private, non-forgeable capability opened by `openVerifiedCreatorHistoricalIssuance()` from a creator-signed aggregate whose author, object, closed epoch, successor epoch and successor anchor all match the independently authenticated floor, a locally stored outbox row is admitted as a REISSUE CANDIDATE when its sequence is nonzero and at most the attested boundary, its scope author and object match the capability, its stored preimage re-encodes canonically, its declared epoch is strictly below the aggregate's closed epoch, and `extractAdmittedReceivedVertex()` verifies the author's own signature, digest and blueprint admission over that preimage. It does not install application state: in recovery the row is counted and skipped (`v3-live.ts:5402-5414`) rather than appended to the journal or graph, unlike the `displaced` class; in the filtered issuance store it merely becomes visible in `readOutboxPage()` when still pending (`v3-live.ts:4863-4888`), which is what surfaces it through `readRebaseOutbox()`. The room then re-derives an application intent, applies the per-action displacement policy (expire, manual-review, transform, rebase), requires a deterministic and identity-stable transform, deduplicates on `(author, action, displacedOperationIdentity)` against already-accepted and imported rows, reissues at a fresh author sequence through the ordinary signed local-issuance transaction under the current ACL and admission policy, and only then calls `completeRebaseSource()`. The row is never published on its stale anchor. Two consequences govern design selection. First, the predicate already accepts an author-signed historical row at or below the attested boundary with no per-sequence digest commitment, and it takes the row's own anchor as `expectedAnchor`, so the incremental authority over the author simply issuing the same operation now is the PROVENANCE claim "the creator admitted this sequence" — which is what makes displacement-policy and identity-dedup semantics meaningful and what keeps a tampered durable store from laundering withheld self-signed rows into the epoch as historical intents. That is why the bare observed maximum is correctly rejected and why no per-gap cryptographic receipt or accumulator is warranted. Second, the classification is also the liveness lever: an outbox row that classifies as none of current, displaced, pinned-genesis or covered-historical makes the entire cold reopen fail with `admission-rejected` (`v3-live.ts:5437-5439`), and recovery iterates every row regardless of `publishState`. So the fact truly required for the consumer and for later cold reopen is only "this sequence was admitted by the creator into an epoch below the closed epoch", expressed so that (a) sequences the creator never observed are never inside the attested set, and (b) sequences the creator did observe remain reachable, and (c) a row outside the attested set yields an explicit per-row refusal rather than aborting the reopen.
structured_output.compatibility_boundary: What f2/f4 actually froze and what I verified is honored: the additive carrier kind `drp-creator-author-issuance-frontiers-state`, domain `ts-drp/creator-author-issuance-frontiers/v1`, version 1, protocolMajor 3, the unchanged 8,192-byte scannable-control ceiling with a 6,241-byte maximum-shape assertion, author-sorted strictly increasing two-element tuples capped at 64 entries with the ACL-derived 256-character objectId grammar, and no change to the v3 vertex wire, digest or signing domains. The legacy `drp-creator-issuance-retirement-state` v1 record stays mandatory; exactly one legacy plus at most one aggregate coexist, with conditional creator equality enforced by the transition verifier on every close and seeding from the legacy carrier only at aggregate 0 to 1. The only exported-surface change is optional and fail-closed: `recoverV3LiveReplica()` accepts exactly base keys, base plus `operationAdmissionPolicy`, base plus `exactCanonicalPinnedGenesisBootstrapOperationBytes`, or base plus both, and `reopenCreatorSuccessorAdoption()` accepts its existing 17 cold keys or those plus the bootstrap policy; the six-key hot activation surface and the 11-key pending-recovery surface are unchanged; absence of the policy yields the existing typed refusal for any pinned-genesis classification, with no permissive fallback. Package-level changes are one `./creator-author-issuance-frontiers` export map entry in `packages/protocol-v3/package.json` and the matching `vite.config.mts` alias; no dependency, lockfile, threshold, memory, timing, workload, archive or Phase-7 change appears in 9e1781e0. The boundary f5 would move, and the reason RED stays unauthorized: the selected covered-run construction adds a third element to each `frontiers` tuple, which changes the canonical signature preimage of that carrier. It needs no new signing authority, no new trust root, no dependency, no public room API change and no threshold change, and because the carrier was introduced in unreleased 9e1781e0 and no room has adopted it, it needs no migration protocol either — but it is still a versioned carrier/schema change and therefore belongs to its own reviewed high-risk prerequisite, with the deterministic maximum-shape encoder re-proving the 64-entry worst case under the unchanged 8,192-byte ceiling before any GREEN, stopping and reslicing rather than raising the ceiling. The close-liveness half of f5 crosses no compatibility boundary at all: leaving a per-author entry unchanged, null, or omitted is already legal in the carrier and already accepted by the transition verifier's monotonicity rule at `packages/node/src/internal/creator-transition-advance.ts:440-445`.
